thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher on Upbeat Jobs Report; Apple's Lackluster iPhone Sales Keep Gains in Check

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher on Upbeat Jobs Report; Apple's Lackluster iPhone Sales Keep Gains in Check
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Friday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +1.5%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.3%
iShares China Large-Cap ETF ( FXI ): +1.6%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.8%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): +0.6%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was down 0.4%.
US stock futures were on track to open higher, fueled by reports that the White House is orchestrating a trade deal with China. Wall Street was also motivated by indicators that the US job market remains strong and wages continue to accelerate, especially following the much awaited jobs data.
The Labor Department reported that 250,000 jobs were created last month, while the unemployment rate remained at 3.7% -- a 48-year low. Forecasts were for an increase of 208,000 in new nonfarm jobs.
The US trade deficit rose 1.3% in September to a seven-month high, widening to $54 billion from a revised $53.3 billion in August. Economists were expecting a $53.6 billion gap. Imports rose 1.5% to a record $266.6 billion; exports also increased 1.5% to $212.6 billion.
In earnings news, Apple (AAPL) logged losses in the pre-market session after the tech giant's better-than-expected Q4 results were overshadowed by broadly flat shipments of its flagship product, the iPhone.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.2% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were flat.
Apple (AAPL) fell more than 6% after it reported Q4 earnings of $2.91 per share, surging 41% over year ago levels and easily beating the analyst consensus of $2.78 per share on Capital IQ. Revenue was $62.9 billion, up 20% over Q4 last year and ahead of expectations of $61.6 billion. For Q1, the company is targeting revenue in the range of $89 to $93 billion, vs. expectations of $92.8 billion. For Q4, the company sold 46.88 million iPhones, flat with year ago levels. Total revenue from iPhone sales was $37.18 billion. Meanwhile, CFO Luca Maestri said on a conference call late Thursday that the company will no longer provide unit sales data for its iPhone product starting with the December quarter. Maestri said: "The number of units sold in any 90-day period is not necessarily representative of the underlying strength of our business."
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 1%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 2.7% while its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 2.6%.
Western Union (WU) rose marginally after it reported late Thursday Q3 adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share, compared with the prior-year period's $0.53 per share. Analysts polled by Capital IQ were expecting EPS of $0.48. Revenue was $1.39 billion, down 1% from $1.4 billion in the same quarter last year. The Street view is for revenue of $1.43 billion. The company now expects fiscal 2018 adjusted EPS of $1.88 - $1.95 versus the Street view is for EPS of $1.85. The prior guidance range was for $1.80 - $1.90.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) was up 1.4% and other funds iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), and Vanguard Industrials (VIS) were quiet.
Universal Display (OLED) fell nearly 26% after it said on Thursday that its second-half is not progressing as expected, as it reported diluted EPS of $0.48 in Q3, up from $0.28 a year earlier, based on new accounting standard ASC 606. Using its previous method, EPS would have been $0.72 for the quarter.
The company reported revenue increased to $77.6 million from $61.7 million in the third quarter of 2017. Revenue would have been $91.6 million without the impact of ASC Topic 606. Analysts expected revenue of $92.21 million and diluted EPS of $0.66 in a Capital IQ poll. For 2018, the company said it now expects revenue of $240 million to $250 million based on new accounting method, against $315 million to $325 million previously using old method. The Street view is for revenue of $304.6 million for the year.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.2% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 1.6% in the pre-market session.
ExxonMobil (XOM) rose more than 2% after the producer of crude oil and natural gas reported Q3 results that topped Wall Street expectations. EPS increased to $1.46 in the September quarter, from $0.93 in the year-ago period. That surpassed the $1.21 average estimate of analysts surveyed by Capital IQ. Q3 revenue increased to $76.61 billion, from $61.1 billion, exceeding the analyst consensus of $72.91 billion.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.3%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.1%. Natural gas was down 1.6% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 2%.
Gold was down 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.1%. Silver was up 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.1%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.3% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 1% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market trade.
Starbucks (SBUX) surged some 8% after it reported Q4 non-GAAP earnings of $0.62 per share, up 13% over year ago levels and two cents better than the analyst consensus on Capital IQ. Revenue was up 11% to $6.3 billion, ahead of expectations of $6.27 billion. Global comparable store sales increased 3%, vs. expectations of 2.5%. For FY 2019, the company expects global comp store sales growth near the low end of its current 3% to 5% range. Revenue growth is seen in the 5% to 7% range. Non-GAAP earnings are targeted at $2.61 to $2.66 per share, vs. estimates of $2.63 per share.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.8% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were quiet. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.8% in pre-market trade.
Pacific Biosciences of California (PACB) soared more than 66% after the company said it agreed to be bought by Illumina (ILMN) for $8 per share in cash. The deal is seen closing in mid-2019. Separately, the company said Q3 sales fell to $18.2 million from $23.5 million in the year-ago period and missed the CapIQ mean for $22.39 million. Net loss per share was $0.19, flat from last year and four cents below forecasts.
